source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Boot into BIOS and check  HDD/ SSD in RAID adapter information correctly.
2. Build raid 0/1/5/6/10/01(base on system / raid card SPEC)
3. Restart system and boot into BIOS to check raid information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Can enter into BIOS without any problems.
2. The raid controller info displays correctly.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Read-only `storcli /c0 show` and `/c0/vall show` over SSH.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: RAID-controller inventory/array info for user confirmation.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; supplies only a read-only controller inventory and neither builds RAID nor proves BIOS display.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; constrains controller, targets, supported RAID subset, backup, recovery and operator BIOS evidence.

original_test_intent: Create each project-supported RAID level from the approved drive population, restart the system, and verify in BIOS that the RAID controller and resulting configuration are represented correctly.
original_method: An approved destructive RAID workflow selects an explicit controller and drive set, builds the supported subset of RAID 0/1/5/6/10/01, restarts once the controller reaches its defined completion state, then a qualified operator enters BIOS and records the displayed RAID information.
manual_activity: The source makes BIOS entry and visual confirmation part of core acceptance. Array creation may be scripted after exact approval, but software output cannot replace the required human BIOS observation; therefore the whole case is MANUAL ONLY.
required_inputs: Controller model/serial/firmware and approved utility version
Drive serial/slot allowlist, current data/boot roles and desired virtual-disk layout
Controller-supported RAID subset and stripe/cache/initialization policy
Explicit one-user destructive approval, backup/reimage plan and maintenance window
OOB console, BIOS path/expected fields and recovery procedure
Engineer decision on build-success and health acceptance missing from Criteria
safety_requirements: Never assume `/c0`; reconcile controller and every drive serial before mutation.
Do not use OS, mounted, in-use, protected, data-bearing or unknown drives without explicit authorization.
Create only the approved RAID subset; do not delete/import/initialize an existing virtual disk unless the unchanged plan explicitly covers it.
Use controller completion/health state rather than a blind delay; no automatic retry or rebuild after failure.
Reboot only with approved OOB recovery; preserve original failures and pre/post controller, OS and SEL evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the immutable controller-drive-layout plan and capture read-only pre-state.
Execute an approved controller-native build command only if the plan explicitly authorizes the exact destructive targets and method.
Monitor documented controller state, collect the full transcript and post-reboot evidence, and report Tool Result separately from engineer verdict.
Do not claim BIOS observation or RAID PASS.
engineer_actions: Approve the destructive target/layout/recovery plan and supported RAID subset.
Perform or directly supervise BIOS navigation and visually attest the expected fields.
Define the missing functional acceptance for each created array and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Insufficient: the two read-only `storcli /c0` queries do not implement any requested RAID build, assume controller 0, and cannot establish BIOS display.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the project-approved controller/BIOS build procedure; use the matching vendor utility for full pre/post inventory and state monitoring only after exact target authorization.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RAID 0/1/5/6/10/01 as supported, restart, BIOS recheck and 15/5-minute fields are preserved; unsupported levels are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONTROLLER-NATIVE APPROVED BUILD PLUS MANUAL BIOS EVIDENCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind controller WWN/serial, enclosure-slot and drive serials in a signed execution manifest; capture machine-readable pre/build/post state and timestamped KVM evidence for each approved RAID level.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact RAID adapter, firmware, drive topology and BIOS.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record controller firmware, BIOS/BMC, OS driver and utility/configuration versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Controller vendor RAID-level, initialization and CLI documentation plus platform BIOS/SIT specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target identity, state-machine monitoring and recoverability without replacing BIOS verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; separates array creation evidence from BIOS display evidence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved topology, RAID parameters and expected functional result.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A visible controller alone does not prove usable, healthy arrays; repeated level builds may destroy prior layouts.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve only the controller-supported RAID subset and a specific drive set. Completion means that approved plan only; it must not be reported as all six source levels when fewer were authorized.
expected_evidence: Pre-state controller/drive identity, existing arrays, boot/mount use and backup/approval
Per-level command or operator transcript, parameters, initialization/health state and resulting VD identity
Reboot/boot evidence and operator-attributed BIOS screenshots for controller and array fields
Post-state controller/OS/BMC/SEL logs, deviations, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure requires building up to six RAID levels, but Criteria checks only BIOS access and controller information. It does not define successful creation, health, capacity, persistence or functional acceptance of any RAID virtual disk. The review cannot silently equate controller visibility with RAID-function success.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The workflow is understandable. Missing topology, approval and functional acceptance are readiness/engineer inputs, not a permanent inability to review or execute an approved project plan.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects YES because read-only inventory omits destructive creation, reboot and BIOS evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its critical target/backup/recovery controls but classifies manual BIOS observation as MANUAL ONLY under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separately exposes the source's missing RAID-build acceptance instead of treating controller display as proof of RAID function.

review_improvement: Prevents a harmless inventory command from masquerading as the test and prevents an array build from being accepted without defined functional criteria.
independent_technical_reasoning: RAID construction is automatable only after exact destructive authorization, but the locked classification follows the core acceptance path: a person must inspect BIOS. The criteria/procedure mismatch is material, yet it is an engineer-decision readiness issue rather than BLOCKED.
no_automatic_retry: Do not retry creation, initialization or reboot automatically. Stop on identity mismatch, unsupported level, degraded drive, controller error or unexpected boot state and preserve all evidence.
